explanation: Zoos have found that a female Komodo dragon can lay eggs that hatch with no male involved, a process called parthenogenesis. Its bite also delivers venom.

claims.text: Komodo dragons, giant lizards of several Indonesian islands, can kill large prey such as deer and water buffalo.
Gila monsters, green iguanas and thorny devils do not live on Indonesian islands or hunt deer and buffalo.
Female Komodo dragons in zoos have produced offspring by parthenogenesis, without mating.
Komodo dragons have venom glands, and their bite delivers venom.

evidence.restatement: Komodo dragons, giant lizards of Komodo, Rinca, Flores and nearby islands, kill deer and water buffalo.
Gila monsters (North America), green iguanas (the Americas) and thorny devils (Australia) neither live wild on Indonesian islands nor hunt deer or buffalo.
Female Komodo dragons in zoos have produced young by parthenogenesis (Watts and colleagues, 2006).
Komodo dragons have venom glands in the lower jaw, and the bite delivers venom (Fry and colleagues, 2009).

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Overall, the glands and toxins are well documented, but whether venom meaningfully contributes to killing prey, beyond the bite itself, is still debated. A 2025 histochemical study confirmed the presence of several types of toxins, though the authors note that a venom depositing and draining structure has yet to be identified in lizard teeth.

claimResults.note: Venom glands in the lower jaw are documented, but sources report that whether the bite delivers venom with a real effect on prey is still debated, and a 2025 study says no venom-delivery structure has been identified in the teeth. Not safe to state as plain fact.

issues.note: checker_doubt c4: the explanation says "Its bite also delivers venom". A search (National Geographic, Wikipedia, a 2025 histology study) shows the venom glands are documented but the role of venom in the bite is debated. Soften to what sources agree on (for example, that it has venom glands) or swap in a settled fact, and re-check c4.
